areas.host: The Electron main process. It owns what a web page cannot do: the window, saving boards, Obsidian vaults, Claude Code, exports, speech, updates.
areas.other: Hooks that run the type check and fast checks while Claude Code edits the repository.
areas.shared: Types and rules both sides rely on: the bridge operations, the card-type table, the board model and the check on Myra’s replies.
areas.static: Static files the page loads as they are: the generated icon pack, the licence text and the offline service worker.
areas.tests: Headless Electron tests, the perf benchmark and fixtures.
areas.tests/smoke: The sections of the end-to-end smoke test, each driving the real app through one area.
areas.tools: Build and project scripts: the bundler, the budget, name and icon generators, notices and the visual diff.
areas.web (root): Renderer entry points: main.ts starts every module in a fixed order, bridge.ts is the way to the host, and the files that draw Myra and the icons.
areas.web/app: First-run setup and tour, the what’s-new card, update checks, start-up and the hooks the tests use.
areas.web/canvas: The board itself: drawing cards, the pointer (drag, resize, connect, pan), copy, paste and drop, connector lines, zoom and view.
areas.web/cards: Behaviour that belongs to one kind of card: collections and kanban, canvases, cropping, links, Spotify, shapes, image fills.
areas.web/content: Starter boards and templates, such as Design thinking and Workshop planning, and the code that places them on a board.
areas.web/core: Foundations everything stands on: DOM handles, the state of the open board, undo and saving, small helpers and colours.
areas.web/docs: Doc cards: the document editor, its menus and toolbar, dropping cards into a doc, Word and PDF export, Myra rewriting a selection.
areas.web/edit: Editing the words on a card, and making a note grow or shrink to fit its text.
areas.web/features: Features that cut across cards: due dates, tags, find, quick capture, focus mode, your own templates, timers, export.
areas.web/library: The left-hand library of projects, folders and boards: opening, renaming, ordering, nesting, deleting, and the home view.
areas.web/media: Audio and video cards: recording, choosing the camera and microphone, stills, and sound extracted for speech.
areas.web/model: The board factory: new boards, the card maker and the bundled templates.
areas.web/myra: Myra herself: her chat, what she can do to the board, greetings, animations, hopping and perching, birthday.
areas.web/panels: The floating panels: Layers, the Unsorted tray and the zoom menu.
areas.web/platform: Things that depend on the device: Mac, Linux or Windows wording, and the phone layout.
areas.web/proto: Prototype boards: the preview, code pane, controls, git bar, building with Myra and keeping code in step with GitHub.
areas.web/repo: Linking a project to a git repo and GitHub, prototyping folders, and starting a prototype from anywhere.
areas.web/richtext: Rich text in notes: the small Markdown a note's text is stored in, its model, and conversion to and from markup, the editor and the clipboard.
areas.web/selbar: The selection bar: colour, text, fill, stroke, corners, arrange and due-date controls for whatever is selected.
areas.web/settings: Settings and looks: colours and themes, widget docking, panel heights, the name-tag cursor, and Myra’s small messages.
areas.web/tools: The tools that make things: pen, ink drawing, shape and stamp pickers, and placing a new card.
areas.web/ui: Shared interface parts: popovers, dialogs, the colour picker, palette, toolbar, minimisable boxes and DOM helpers.
areas.web/vault: Obsidian vault support in the page: connecting vaults, who may read them, vault note cards, and notes or tasks gathered for Myra.
areas.web/wireframe: Wireframe design: the elements Myra and you place, screens, the Pieces picker, sections, stacking order and tilt.

files.tools/flakes-gh.ts: The only code that asks GitHub for the ledger: runs gh and checks what comes back into runs and attempt-1 failures.
files.tools/flakes-ledger.ts: The CI ledger over values already read: which runs needed a rerun, whether the same commit then passed, the counts and the table.
files.tools/flakes-log.ts: Reads a failed attempt’s log into the test files and jobs that failed, each with its first failing line.
files.tools/flakes.ts: Prints how often CI needed a rerun in the last n days, what failed on the first attempt and whether the same commit then passed.
files.tools/icons.ts: Builds the icon pack and the list of names Myra may use.
files.tools/icons/set.ts: Maps each Myra icon name to a drawing in the current icon pack.
files.tools/licence-check.ts: Fails when Fenmyr's own licence is named differently in package.json, LICENSE, NOTICE, the docs, About and the two generated notice files.
files.tools/make-icon.ts: Draws the app icon and the browser tab icon.
files.tools/metrics.ts: Counts files and lines of code per area of the project.
files.tools/notices.ts: Writes the third-party notices and the licences list.
files.tools/shortcuts-doc.ts: Writes docs/shortcuts.md from the toolbar table and the keymap, and fails in check:fast when the page is out of date.
files.tools/sleeps.ts: Finds the fixed sleeps in a test file for the budget: waitForTimeout, T.wait, a promise on setTimeout and settle(page, ms), minus those marked as the point of the test.
files.tools/readme-art.ts: Writes the README's art: Myra as looping animated PNGs drawn by her own sprite, and the heading icons in cloudberry colours.
files.tools/readme-shots.ts: Takes the README's screenshots, the example board and a built prototype board in light and dark, scaled for GitHub.
files.tools/run-tests.ts: Runs every test in tests/ or the ones named, each alone and past failures, and one CI shard of them balanced on recorded times.
files.tools/visual-channels.ts: The visual states for Settings → About with the Channel row, on a release and on a beta, with the update check answered as a clone install answers it.
files.tools/visual-diff.ts: Screenshots 22 states here and on main, and fails on any changed pixel.
files.tools/visual-guides.ts: The visual states for a new prototype’s rules and design cards: the board with them, the doc view of its rules, and the Ignore switch on, in light and dark.
files.tools/visual-homeempty.ts: Home with nothing in a level as visual states: a project with no folder, a folder with no board, no project in dark, and a folder with no board in a phone-width window.
files.tools/visual-newproject.ts: The New project dialog as a visual state: over the board in light, with a search, in dark and in a phone-width window.
files.tools/visual-myra.ts: Myra’s states for the visual diff: a reply in the open chat, what she sees, the chat and doc panels, and a plan with its board preview, before and after Do it.
files.tools/visual-wireframe.ts: The wireframe board's states for the visual diff: the screen tool, a selected screen, the Pieces picker and its Icons view, an empty screen's hint, and the picker in dark and on a phone.
files.tools/visual-proto.ts: The prototype board’s states for the visual diff: a fresh repo’s board at three widths and in dark, its chat at its narrowest, and its git bar’s More menu open.
files.web/boot.js: Sets the native class before the page paints, so the desktop app makes room for its window buttons.
files.web/sw.js: Keeps a copy of the app so the website version opens offline.
files.tests/cardInk.ts: The words on every colour of note, and on a doc, read on the card in every theme, so a light Snow card in Lantern has dark text.
files.tests/cardNames.ts: A card's accessible name says what it is and its colour's name in every theme, so people who can't see the colour get the cue Clear and Lantern print on the card.
files.tests/noteTabOrder.ts: Tab and Shift+Tab walk a note's title, body and label in that order, keep a list item's Tab for indent, and leave the card at either end.
files.tests/noteNamelessStart.ts: A double-click on the words of a note with no name types in the words; the empty name line shows only once the note is being typed in.
files.tests/themeBoards.ts: A board saved under Clear holds colour keys and no theme colour, and opens under every theme with that theme's own fill on each card.
files.tests/colourLabels.ts: Clear and Lantern print a note's colour name on it and no other theme does, and the label doesn't change the note's size.
files.tests/cardExtras.ts: Clear and Lantern draw a border-colour outline in every card and sit their cards straight, a stamp keeping its tilt; other themes are unchanged and the outline moves nothing.
files.src/web/settings/boardsSaved.ts: The bold line on Settings, General: the board count, then Locally saved or, when a project is linked to a repo, Local files linked to a remote repo.
files.src/web/settings/derivedModes.ts: The area colours that differ between light and dark, as expressions of the core tokens, which style.css reads instead of a body.dark rule.
files.tests/boardLists.ts: A board file written by hand with no card list and no tray opens as an empty board instead of failing to load.
files.tests/boardsSaved.ts: Settings, General shows the board count with Locally saved, or Local files linked to a remote repo once a project is linked, and a note under it that Myra and a repo send information along.
files.tests/contextFit.ts: Tests that what Myra is sent from a board follows the model’s window, is cut in ranked order, and says every cut in words.
files.tests/dueCues.ts: An overdue chip has its own icon and says Overdue, so its red is not the only cue; a chip that turns overdue while the board is open gets both, and one that is not overdue keeps the clock.
files.src/web/settings/shortcutList.ts: The Keyboard shortcuts list in Settings → Board: a block per group with its entries, each a description and its keys in a keycap.
